#           time_to_unlock u64 }
#         per_subaddress_info = { account_index u32, address_index u32, address string, balance u64,

# NO status/untrusted: the WALLET RPC has no rpc_response_base. Only the DAEMON's responses carry
#         `status`, which is why DESIGN.md §1b.3's BUSY rule is a node rule and not a wallet rule.
# request: { account_index, address_indices, all_accounts (OPT false, :71), strict (OPT false, :72) }
# per_subaddress HOLDS ONLY FUNDED SUBADDRESSES. wallet2::balance_per_subaddress builds it from
#         subaddresses holding unspent, unfrozen outputs (src/wallet/wallet2.cpp:7037-7060), so this
#         fixture deliberately carries ONE entry while get_address.json carries THREE addresses. That
#         asymmetry is the point: DESIGN.md §5 sources status.wallet.subaddress_count from
#         get_address.addresses.len() (3) and NOT from per_subaddress.len() (1), and §7a's Wallet
#         screen joins the two, rendering an em dash where a subaddress has no row here.
# AMOUNTS ARE PICONERO INTEGERS (1 XMR = 1e12, src/cryptonote_config.h:66-67). balance 1234567891234
#         = "1.234567891234" XMR, the worked example of DESIGN.md §5, so this fixture and §5's
#         document cannot disagree and Piconero::to_xmr_string's round trip is exercised on it.
# blocks_to_unlock / time_to_unlock are 0 here (nothing locked), so the wallet_locked_funds warning
#         (§5) does NOT fire; get_balance-locked.json is the fixture that makes it fire.
# time_to_unlock IS SECONDS and is named time_to_unlock on the wire (:98, :117) while DESIGN.md §5
#         renders it as status.wallet.time_to_unlock_sec -- the `_sec` suffix is fmonero's, not
#         Monero's.

#         subaddress tests/functional_tests/validate_address.py:73 (mainnet subaddress, prefix 42)
#         See tests/fixtures/address-forms.json for all nine forms and their provenance.
